Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 01/27/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 21 as introduced statutorily authorizes the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to set fees by rule. This would allow the board to continue charging a license verification fee and a Center for Credentialing & Education (CCE) provider/course approval application fee while also allowing the board to establish fees for other services. The board receives approximately $40,000 to $60,000 in annual collections to the Board of Chiropractic Examiners Fund in the State Treasury from the license verification fee and the CCE provider/course approval fee collectively. Any additional fees for other services established by the board pursuant to this bill would increase collections to the Board of Chiropractic Examiners Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the rate adopted by the board and the frequency the fee is paid.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 02/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 21 as passed the Senate codifies the current practice of the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners by authorizing the board to charge and collect certain fees by rule. This bill would allow the board to continue charging a license verification fee of $12.50 each, and a fee to act as a continuing education provider at $75 per module, while also allowing the board to establish fees for other services. The board collects approximately $50,000 annually for these two fees.
Howard Sanderford, Chair
Boards, Agencies and Commissions
